topic_brief.title: Organic vs conventional farming crop yield gap
topic_brief.research_question: How much lower is crop yield under organic farming compared to conventional farming?
topic_brief.population_description: Crop plants grown in field experiments comparing farming systems
topic_brief.intervention_description: Organic farming system (certified organic or following organic principles: no synthetic fertilizers, no synthetic pesticides)
topic_brief.comparator_description: Conventional farming system (using synthetic fertilizers and/or pesticides)
topic_brief.outcome_description: Crop yield (grain, fruit, or total biomass harvested per unit area)
tc_confusion_warnings: Treatment is ORGANIC (lower input), Control is CONVENTIONAL (higher input)
Some papers compare 3+ systems (organic, integrated, conventional) - extract organic vs conventional only
Low-input is NOT the same as organic unless explicitly stated
Transitional organic may show different effects than established organic - record years since conversion
Watch for factorial designs (organic x irrigation) - extract each organic vs conventional at same irrigation level
topic_brief.benchmark_source: Ponisio et al. 2015 (Proc R Soc B 282:20141396)

rows.title: Effect of organic farming practices on soil and performance of soybean (Glycine max) under semi-arid tropical conditions in Central India
rows.treatment_description: Organic farming practice (cattle dung manure on N-equivalent basis, rock phosphate for P, neem oil for pest control)
rows.control_description: Chemical/inorganic farming practice (chemical fertilizers and recommended pesticides)
rows.notes: Data is mean of 2 years (2011-2012). LSD is for management effect at P<0.05. Organic yield was HIGHER than conventional, opposite to typical yield gap literature. Soybean is a legume which may benefit more from organic N via biological fixation.
